title: Interview Arcade
summary: Technical interview practice tool that takes code and audio input, evaluates both, and returns spoken feedback.
thumb_alt: The Interview Arcade welcome screen, reading "Welcome to Interview Arcade!" above Company, Random and Category buttons and a Confirm button.

title: C-PORT
summary: Web-based analytics platform that optimises portfolios of offshore energy technologies across a stretch of coast, instead of assessing each technology in isolation.
thumb_alt: The C-PORT web interface: a Portfolio Optimization panel with resource upload and a North Carolina location preset, beside a Technicals panel of transmission, depth, distance and cost-of-energy inputs.
status: 1st place, undergraduate research poster — NCROEP Symposium

title: OutSource
summary: Weather-aware activity planning: live forecasts plus AI recommendations for when to get outside, with circles, friends and a shared schedule to organise it.
thumb_alt: The OutSource home screen: an orange Current Forecast card reading 45 degrees and clear, above personal recommendations for a day hike and a park visit that both cite the sunny weather.

title: SLCCE Workshop Platform
summary: Hosting platform that lets students run interactive computing lessons in the browser, built for an NC State volunteer organization teaching middle and high school students.
thumb_alt: The workshop platform's home page: a teal banner reading "Learn to code, right in your browser", with buttons to browse workshops or start with a how-to guide.

title: Pounce
summary: Multiplayer solitaire as a real-time web app, built in four staged sub-projects over roughly a year.
thumb_alt: The Pounce game board, with several players’ solitaire layouts of face-up and face-down cards arranged around a shared centre area.

title: Competitive Programming
summary: An ongoing record of contests, ratings and the problem-solving techniques picked up along the way.
thumb_alt: A LeetCode profile page showing a contest rating of 2,013 at Knight level, in the top 2.47% globally.

title: Typing
summary: Ten years of chasing two typing goals — 200 wpm over 15 seconds and 180 wpm over 60 — and finally hitting both.
thumb_alt: A Monkeytype result screen: 208 words per minute at 96% accuracy on a 15-second English test.

title: The Write Place
summary: Android app and companion website where students upload essays, exchange feedback and search by tag.
thumb_alt: The Write Place logo, a pencil drawn inside a house outline, beside the sign-in form with email, username and password fields.

title: Builder Base Guide Website
summary: A self-directed static guide site for a Clash of Clans game mode, written for friends to use.
thumb_alt: A Clash of Clans Builder Base profile screen showing 5000 trophies, an all-time best of 7091, and a best tournament finish of 36th in the April 2022 season.

title: Chip's Challenge
summary: A planning agent that collects every chip and reaches the portal using a subtask stack and A* search.
thumb_alt: The Chip’s Challenge grid, showing the player character surrounded by computer chips, coloured keys and locked doors, with "Chips Remaining 10" beside the board.

title: 10x Escape
summary: A JavaFX puzzle game inspired by 40x Escape, with faithful level recreations and original puzzles.
thumb_alt: A 10x Escape puzzle level on a teal background, with a black panel, a row of lettered buttons and the caption "Level 10".

title: Conway's Game of Life
summary: A Java GUI for Conway's Game of Life with preset and custom configurations, including a hand-rebuilt glider gun.
thumb_alt: A Game of Life grid mid-simulation, filled with scattered black live cells in small clusters.

title: Inverted Dartboard
summary: Computed the expected value of a dart throw on an inverted board by hand, then checked it against a Monte Carlo simulation.
thumb_alt: Two dartboards side by side, labelled Board A and Board B. Board A is a standard numbered board; Board B has plain concentric rings scoring 10 at the outside up to 80 at the centre.

title: Covid Simulation
summary: A Python Turtle epidemic model with flu and plague modes, distance-based transmission and a matplotlib summary.
thumb_alt: The simulation running in a Python Turtle window, a grid of green, yellow and red circles at week 20, beside a matplotlib graph of infected and dead percentages over time.
